_what: Synthetic Ruby block-parameter gate for #3905 (RUBY-03), following bench/ruby-gem-resolution: exact accuracy cells and fingerprints, with ratios as the only timing gates. Real capture emitter, real parse worker (dist/), real Ruby ScopeResolver and manifest loader; analyze, persistence and full-pipeline memory are outside this benchmark.
_triage: Shape and fingerprint failures are deterministic: inspect the corpus and the resolved edges, never rebaseline just to make CI green. The runner also fails, before any baseline comparison, when a method misses an expected CALLS edge or gains one the source never makes. For a timing failure, rerun on an idle machine and verify the report shows its profile (ci: 5 interleaved samples after 1 warmup; full: 15 after 2) before investigating a regression. Millisecond observations are context, not gates.
_shape_note: Exact counts are the workload FLOOR. small = 64 methods x 6 blocks, large = 256 x 6 (methods 4x); dense = 64 x 96 side by side (blocks per method 16x) and 64 x 24 nested (depth 4x; see _nested_depth_note). Every line has a fixed-width indent, so input_bytes (pinned per shape) grows linearly in methods and in blocks: 25047 -> 100083 (large, 4.0x), 305367 (sibling dense, 12.2x for 16x blocks) and 81111 (nested dense, 3.2x for 4x depth); with the earlier two-spaces-per-level indent nested input grew 6.1x for 4x depth. One class with one method per file. Expected edges per method are computed from the binder rule, not read back from the graph: a block that rebinds `user` (`|user|`, `|user, i|`) gets no edge, `|x|` reaches the nearest `user` (the local `User` unless an enclosing block rebinds it), and the closing `user.save` reaches User#save. main misses that rule (128 wrong edges at 32 x 6 side by side), so this gate fails without #3905. The one `member-lookup-ambiguous` decline per method is identical on main.
_fingerprint_note: Hashes pin every relationship (endpoints, type, confidence, reason) and every decline (reason, file, name, position).
_scaling_note: Scaling ratios are (t_dense / t_small) / growth and (t_large / t_small) / 4, where growth is 16 for sibling blocks and 4 for nesting depth: about 1 is linear, about the growth factor is quadratic. 1.5 (bench/scope-capture) on every ratio.
_one_file_note: Not gated: on main, Ruby resolution is super-linear in the number of classes or methods in ONE file. With every class in one file (`--shape crowded`), 256 -> 2048 methods, resolution's fitted exponent is 1.60 (1.48-1.72) on main and 1.61 (1.52-1.70) with #3905, per-doubling ratios 2.8 -> 3.5 on both; in a profile at 2048 classes the time is in ruby/merge-bindings.ts and in findClassBindingInScope / lookupMatchingNameClaim (scope-resolution/scope/walkers.ts). #3905 changes neither, and its absolute time there is lower (1180 vs 1641 ms at 2048). The gated shapes therefore use one class per file.
_profiles_note: Two profiles share the shapes and every accuracy gate. CI (the default, and what --check runs in the benchmarks job): one process, one parse worker, every workload timed, min of 5 after 1 warmup, interleaved. --full: one child times every workload, min of 15 after 2 warmups, and each shape runs in a fresh child for its peak RSS. Wall times are in _measured_ci.
_negative_controls_note: Walking the enclosing method once per block scope (O(blocks^2) per method, a temporary edit of attachRubyLexicalNames in languages/ruby/captures.ts) fails sibling_capture_block_scaling_ratio 3.596 > 1.5 (nested 1.778) in the CI profile, with unchanged fingerprints. With the earlier 4x side-by-side range the same edit gave 1.410 and passed: per-file overhead hid it, which is why that range is now 16x. These are deliberate regressions, not baseline observations.

_measured_ci.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 23-80 on 15 cores)

_measured_full.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 23-80 on 15 cores)

_measured_note: Three CI-profile runs and one --full run on 382d254dc with this runner. Scalar ratios and millisecond values are per-metric maxima across the runs of that profile (rounded); the 84 s wall time is one run under load average ~80, the others took 24-25 s. peak_rss_mib (--full only) is each --shape child's high-water mark after one worker parse and one resolution, worker thread included; context, not gated. Exact shapes and fingerprints were identical in all runs. Shapes changed from the earlier runner: fixed-width indent (nested decline positions, hence nested fingerprints) and 96 blocks per sibling method.
_rebaselined_on_main: Rebased #3905 onto 14d5405a5 after #3903 and #3880 merged. All six workloads retain their capture groups, CALLS, relationship counts, and zero missing/unexpected edges. DART-11 now records receiver-type-unresolved/untyped-binder declines: sibling small/large/dense 640/2560/2560; nested small/large/dense 704/2816/3008. Only those recorded declines and their fingerprints change; the pre-existing member-lookup-ambiguous counts and all scaling budgets are unchanged. Measured scaling ratios range from 0.692 to 1.056, below 1.5.
_nested_depth_note: Nesting depth stays 4x (6 -> 24). Over 6 -> 96 on this head (CI profile, one run, fixed-width indent) nested_capture_block_scaling_ratio is 2.57 and nested_resolve_block_scaling_ratio 2.46, from two terms that predate #3905: capture, the shared callable-flow fallback that searches a block-taking call's whole subtree for an argument list (`items.each do ... end` has none; O(depth^2), fixed for Ruby in the bare-read follow-up to #3880); resolution, the shared lexical lookup that climbs from each reference to its binder (`items` at every level climbs to the method; O(depth^2)). Widen the nested range when those land.
